newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bank SKB 1996 net profit up.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bank SKB 1996 net profit up.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank SKB said on Monday its 1996 consolidated net profit rose to 1.79 billion tolars ($11.6 million) from 713 million according to international accounting standards.
The bank said earlier its net profit had risen to 1.48 billion tolars ($9.6 million) from 602 million when calculated by Slovenian standards.
The bank said profits were up mainly because of improved interest margins and expanded tolar and foreign currency operations involving both individuals and companies.

"The biggest rise (of operations) was recorded in the area of loans to individuals which were up by 23 percent, while financial cross-border transactions rose by seven percent," chief executive Ivan Nerad told a news conference.
According to international accounting standards, SKB's balance sheet assets rose to 208.3 billion tolars ($1.35 billion) in 1996 from 178.6 billion a year earlier.
"Last year we improved the quality of our balance sheet assets and opened six new branches in Slovenia, thus taking the number of branches to 54," Nerad said.
He said the bank had not yet determined the dividend for 1996, but expected it to be slightly higher than the 1,100 tolars per share paid last year.
Nerad said SKB expected to increase its market share in Slovenia to 16 percent by 2000, up from its current 11.2 percent share.
In February, SKB became the first Slovenian company to be traded abroad, listing its global depositary receipts (GDRs) on the London and Munich stock exchanges.
"The GDR offer was very successful because the demand for GDRs exceeded the offer by about 27 times," board member Cvetka Selsek said.
The GDRs, representing 29 percent of SKB's equity, are currently trading at about 110,000 tolars, while SKB shares traded in Ljubljana eased 1.17 percent to 59,000 tolars on Monday.
